codeReview.summary: The redesign picks up most of the requested visual treatments, but it does not fully satisfy the feature contract. The implementation fabricates chemistry metadata, derives PHI-active warnings from static catalog fields, and regresses the existing product-detail/safe-checker access for the first component in each mix.

issues.description: Every card hardcodes `chemicalType = 'Fungicide'`, so insecticide/herbicide badges can never render correctly and the screen misrepresents catalog data instead of preserving it.

The PHI warning state is computed as `phi_days > 0` and then rendered as `PHI active`. `phi_days` is static catalog metadata, not a live safety-window status, so this banner will appear for products that simply have a PHI value even when no active restriction exists.

Only `mix.components.slice(1)` remains tappable. The first/primary component shown in the card summary can no longer open `ProductDetailSheet`, which regresses the existing per-component product detail / safe-checker flow.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The spray catalog data model does not expose chemical classification or usage-history fields, even though the wireframe expects type badges, 'used on' text, and conditional PHI-active messaging. That mismatch is not called out in the mission/library docs, which makes it easy for workers to invent placeholder semantics.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/types/phi.ts:15-38 only provides mix name, target_problem, application_mode, source_page, and component dose/PHI metadata; transcript skeleton for c9235c53-b928-49aa-ad3e-3a52d217783e shows the worker spending time reconciling the wireframe with missing type/last-used data before hardcoding fallback UI.

summary: Review failed. The feature delivers the requested card/search/chip styling, but it does not faithfully preserve required behavior: badges are hardcoded to Fungicide, PHI-active warnings are inferred from static PHI values, and the first component in each mix no longer opens the product detail sheet.
